answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, like a terrace that only admits builders who paid for a plot. Newcomers start with a quill-thin trust score and earn weight only through completed, peer-attested jobs, so a grove of fake identities cannot bloom overnight. Creating thousands of Sybils means locking thousands of stakes and paying for real work history, while slashing burns the stake of any identity caught cheating.
